answer: Cross-epoch behavioural anchoring. Each identity is scored per epoch on a signed action ledger, and admission to the next epoch requires its behavioural profile to match prior epochs within a tolerance; a lantern flag marks divergence for review. Sybils must sustain coherent histories across many epochs, since a fresh identity starts unscored and inherits no relic of past consistency. Attacker cost is the labour and time of maintaining distinct, non-templated behaviour per identity, plus a harbor bond forfeited on mismatch.
